newsitem.title: USA: Pilots adjourn American talks, set April 3 meeting.
newsitem.headline: Pilots adjourn American talks, set April 3 meeting.

text.p: Union pilots on Saturday adjourned without a decision a meeting held to consider whether to approve a new contract proposal with American Airlines, and scheduled another meeting on April 3, a spokesman said.

The board of the Allied Pilots Association met for two days to hear a report by its negotiating committee on the proposal, part of a bid to avert a threatened strike by 9,000 pilots working for American, a unit of AMR Corp..

Union spokesman Wally Pitts said the meeting was adjourned to give the negotiators time to put the agreement in principle on the contract proposal into legal language which was required for board action.
He said the April meeting was set for two days, at a site not yet decided. The APA and American are working against an April 28 strike deadline.

The major stumbling block to the agreement is who is to fly new commuter planes American plans to buy -- APA pilots, who make an average of $120,000 a year, or pilots of American's commuter line, American Eagle, who make about $35,000.

Union President James Sovich said earlier that the APA had reached an understanding with the Air Line Pilots Association, which represents Eagle pilots, on cockpit rights, but that American Airlines had not yet signed on to the understanding.
